ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point a
ev.original: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.justification: Motor vehicles should be fully exempted from the mandatory low-carbon steel and aluminium requirements established under Annex II and related provisions. Any future requirements for automotive materials should be considered only after: the applicable definitions and calculation methodologies have been finalised;·sufficient volumes of qualifying automotive-grade materials are demonstrably available; technical feasibility and safety have been independently assessed; and·the cost and administrative implications for vehicle manufacturers and consumers have been duly evaluated.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point a
ev.original: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)For steel products, components and assembled final products containing steel, Union origin shall be established only where the steel has been melted and poured in the customs territory of the Union. The rules on melt and pour laid down in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1963, including the rules concerning the evidence required to establish the country of melt and pour, shall apply to the determination and verification of Union origin under this Regulation. Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel falling under CN chapters 72 and 73, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 50% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon and of Union origin;

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point a
ev.original: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 15% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon; from 1 January 2033, or three years after the date on which the requirement laid down in the first part of this point becomes applicable, whichever is later, that share shall be at least 25%, provided that the Commission, in a review carried out pursuant to Article 29 and completed not earlier than 18 months before that date, has established that the supply of low-carbon steel in the Union is sufficient to meet that share without disproportionate price increases for contracting authorities and beneficiaries;
ev.justification: A gradual increase gives steelmakers time to build low-carbon capacity and limits early price premiums for public budgets. The higher share should apply only after a recent review has positively confirmed that supply and prices allow it, rather than automatically unless a shortage is found, so that public buyers are never bound by a target the market cannot meet.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point a
ev.original: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings and infrastructure at least 50% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon and of Union origin (melted and poured in the EU and labelled as low-carbon on the basis of product-category-specific greenhouse gas emissions intensity thresholds that shall not be adjusted through a sliding-scale mechanism or any equivalent mechanism); if intended for use in motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.justification: It is proposed to increase to 50% the minimum share of low-carbon steel of European origin in public procurement and other incentives and support schemes, given that 25% coverage in the construction sector would represent less than 5% of total steel demand.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point a
ev.original: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon; where Union origin requirements apply to steel under this Regulation, the origin of steel shall be determined by the country in which it was originally melted and poured, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2026/1384, and steel deemed to be of Union origin pursuant to Article 8 shall be treated as being of Union origin;

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point a
ev.original: (a)Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)Steel, cast iron and steel used in any product for which steel accounts for 10% or more in weight, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure, NZIA technologies including wind energy projects and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 50% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon and of Union Origin. Only steel that has been originally melted and poured within the Union, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 shall qualify as being of Union origin;
ev.justification: Europe must create demand for low-carbon steel produced in the EU, ensuring decarbonisation supports European investment, jobs and industrial capacity rather than imports. Public procurement and support schemes should require Union-origin steel, defined by “Melt and Pour”. A 50% quota would strengthen demand by 2030, while a 10% steel-content threshold would improve legal certainty and reduce administrative burdens. Wind should be included in NZIA criteria. During the transition, flexibility for imported DRI/HBI is essential to preserve competitiveness and EU supply chains.

ev.amended: (a)Steel and iron, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure, including water pipes, and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon and of Union origin; this percentage shall progressively rise according to the following: 25% from 1 January 2029, 35% from 1 January 2032, 50% from 1 January 2036;
ev.justification: Ductile iron shares with steel a comparable decarbonisation pathway, based on the progressive replacement of blast furnaces by electric arc furnaces. Including iron alongside steel in the scope of this Annex ensures consistency across industrial materials following similar transition trajectories.Water pipes represent the main outlet for ductile iron and a market significantly exposed to public procurement, in particular through investments by Member States and local authorities in water supply and sanitation infrastructure. Their explicit inclusion ensures that this Regulation effectively supports the decarbonisation of the European ductile iron industry and reinforces the resilience of a strategic value chain for water infrastructure.

ev.justification: Union primary aluminium capacity has shrunk and the market for low-carbon aluminium is still forming. ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point c a (new)
ev.amended: (ca)tyres for fitting to motor vehicles for civil use, including replacement tyres for in-service vehicles: at least 70 % of the total number of tyres purchased must be of Union origin; this percentage shall be raised to 85 % as from 1 January 2032; class C1 and C2 tyres shall be at least class B for fuel efficiency and class B for wet grip within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2020/740; for class C3, re-treaded tyres of EU origin shall be taken into account for the purpose of meeting these percentages.
ev.justification: Replacement accounts for around 75 % of European tyre manufacturers’ sales. Limiting the requirements to new vehicles would not create a lead market. Extra-EU imports increased from EUR 880 million in 2010 to EUR 1.36 billion in 2024, and European manufacturers have lost 12 % of market share since 2018. Labelling requirements also ensure energy and safety gains.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point c a (new)
ev.amended: (ca)foundry products and cast components of iron, copper, zinc and magnesium, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure, net-zero technologies and motor vehicles for civil purposes: a minimum share of such products and components, to be specified in accordance with Article 16(2), shall be low-carbon and of Union origin.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point c a (new)
ev.amended: (ca)cast and forged products and components made of iron, copper, zinc or magnesium, intended for use in buildings and infrastructure excluding energy grids and energy grid infrastructure, and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% share of such products and components shall be low-carbon and of Union origin.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point c a (new)
ev.amended: (ca)rubber products designed for use in motor vehicles, including as replacement parts, namely hoses, belts, tyres and retreaded tyres, where the weight of rubber or rubber components accounts for more than 20% of the total weight of the component in which they are incorporated, shall be low-carbon and of Union origin.
ev.justification: Hoses, belts and tyres are produced by an energy-intensive industry listed in Annex I and are essential to vehicle safety and efficiency. Tyres replacement market accounts for 75% of EU tyre sales and is the segment most exposed to imports, which rose from EUR 881 million in 2010 to EUR 1 360 million in 2024. Retreading truck and bus tyres in the Union saves materials and roughly halves emissions compared with producing new tyres.

ev.article: Annex II – Part I – paragraph 1 – point c b (new)
ev.amended: (cb)cast and foundry products made of steel, iron or aluminium are covered by the relevant Union-origin and low-carbon requirements when incorporated into vehicles, infrastructure and net-zero technology products.

ev.original: For schemes established or updated on or after 1 January 2029 that benefit households or companies and that primarily aim to support the construction or renovation of buildings for residential and commercial purposes and infrastructure and the lease and purchase of motor vehicles for civil purposes, Member States, regional or local authorities, bodies governed by public law or associations formed by one or more such authorities or one or more such bodies governed by public law, shall ensure that only beneficiaries that comply with the following minimum requirements, are eligible.
ev.amended: For schemes established or updated on or after 1 January 2030, or three years after the entry into force of the delegated act referred to in Article 10(1) for the product concerned, whichever is later, that benefit households or companies and that primarily aim to support the construction or renovation of buildings for residential and commercial purposes and infrastructure and the lease and purchase of motor vehicles for civil purposes, Member States, regional or local authorities, bodies governed by public law or associations formed by one or more such authorities or one or more such bodies governed by public law, shall ensure that only beneficiaries that comply with the following minimum requirements, are eligible. This Part shall not apply to schemes whose beneficiaries are natural persons building or renovating their own dwelling or housing communities or housing cooperatives renovating residential buildings.
ev.justification: Asking a family renovating its home, or a housing cooperative, to document the carbon intensity and origin of the steel, cement or aluminium used is unrealistic. It would add costs and paperwork for households and small contractors while barely affecting demand. Large public and commercial projects are the right lever, and the start date follows the availability of the methodology. Schemes for vulnerable households and social housing are left to Member States under Article 12.

ev.justification: The minimum thresholds should not create bottlenecks or disproportionate cost increases that could undermine project competitiveness. The targets should be phased in progressively in line with European production capacity, which should be monitored in advance and strengthened through policies supporting investment and industrial development.

ev.article: Annex II – Part II – point a
ev.original: (a)steel, and any product the performance of which depends primarily on steel : at least 25% of the total volume of steel used in the product or project that receives support shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings and infrastructure at least 50% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon and of Union origin (melted and poured in the EU and labelled as low-carbon on the basis of product-category-specific greenhouse gas emissions intensity thresholds that shall not be adjusted through a sliding-scale mechanism or any equivalent mechanism); if intended for use in motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;
ev.justification: It is proposed to increase to 50% the minimum share of low-carbon steel of European origin in public procurement and other incentives and support schemes, given that 25% coverage in the construction sector would represent less than 5% of total steel demand.

ev.article: Annex II – Part II – point a
ev.original: (a)steel, and any product the performance of which depends primarily on steel : at least 25% of the total volume of steel used in the product or project that receives support shall be low-carbon;
ev.amended: (a)steel, cast iron, cast iron pipes and steel used in any product for which steel accounts for 10% or more in weight: at least 50% of the total volume of steel or cast iron used in the product or project that receives support shall be low-carbon and of Union Origin. Only steel that has been originally melted and poured within the Union, in accordance with Regulation (EU 2026/1384) shall qualify as being of Union origin;
ev.justification: Cast iron is an integral part of strategic European manufacturing value chains, supplying key components for automotive, energy, infrastructure and industrial applications. It should therefore benefit from the same demand-side requirements applicable to steel.

ev.amended:
New pure electric vehicles (PEV) or off-vehicle charging hybrid electric vehicles (OVC-HEV) purchased, leased, rented or hire-purchased in public procurement procedures that fall within the scope of Directive 2014/24/EU, or Directive 2014/25/EU, launched on or after [OP: Please insert the date = six months after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] shall comply with the Union origin requirements set out in this Annex.
By way of derogation from this paragraph, fuel cell vehicles (FCV) of category M1 or N1, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall be excluded from those requirements.
ev.justification: Fuel cell vehicles remain at an early stage of market deployment and depend on hydrogen refuelling infrastructure that is not yet sufficiently developed across the Union. Applying the vehicle origin requirements to FCVs at this stage would create disproportionate compliance obligations without delivering meaningful industrial benefits. The scope should therefore be limited to technologies with established or rapidly scaling market uptake, while allowing additional time for the hydrogen mobility ecosystem to mature.

ev.original: New PEV, OVC-HEV and FCV that are used for the provision of services sourced through public procurement procedures that fall within the scope of Directive 2014/24/EU, or Directive 2014/25/EU, shall comply with the Union origin requirements set out in this Annex.
ev.amended: New zero and low emission vehicles, including vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels (VEEF), that are used for the provision of services sourced through public procurement procedures that fall within the scope of Directive 2014/24/EU, or Directive 2014/25/EU, shall comply with the Union origin requirements set out in this Annex.
ev.justification: Union origin requirements should apply on a technologically neutral basis to all zero- and low-emission vehicles, including vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels. This ensures that European industrial policy supports all technologies capable of contributing to transport decarbonisation.

ev.original: Vehicles referred to in subparagraphs 1 and 2 shall include the following Union origin requirements:
ev.amended: Vehicles referred to in subparagraphs 1 and 2 shall include all of the following Union origin requirements:

ev.amended: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union, including all stages of the vehicle’s final assembly;

ev.amended: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union or a partner country as defined in Article 7;
ev.justification: Vehicles assembled in a partner country count towards the "made in the EU" criteria, in line with Article 7.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point a
ev.original: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union as provided for in Article 7(1) and (1a);

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point a
ev.original: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union or in the United Kingdom ;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the battery – is at least 70%;
ev.amended:
(b)6 months after entry into force: the ratio between the total ex-works price of the vehicle - excluding the ex-works price of the vehicle battery - minus the sum of the total ex-works price of the non-originating components, and the total ex-works price of the vehicle originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the vehicle battery – is at least 50%;
3 years after entry into force: the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle minus the sum of the total ex-works price of the non-originating components and the total ex-works price of the vehicle – is equal to or greater than 70%.
ev.justification: The current proposal calculates "made in EU" content solely on the basis of component value, failing to capture the full scope of European value creation. Activities performed in Europe are totally dismissed, including R&D, software development, system integration (powertrain, chassis, electronics, software), production-linked value (engineering, tooling, testing), quality, safety and compliance.Regarding batteries, the amendments aim to align Union origin requirements with the current industrial capacity and economic reality of the EU battery value chain.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the battery – is at least 70%;
ev.amended:
(b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the battery – is at least 80%.
For the purpose of this calculation, the value of materials used for the production of those components, in particular materials covered under Annex I or II, shall be taken into account and shall be considered as originating in the Union only where those materials are produced in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the battery – is at least 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total added value of vehicle - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total added value of the vehicle – excluding the battery – is at least 70%. This should include cast parts incorporated into higher-tier components;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point b

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point b

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point b

ev.justification: The calculation of Union industrial content should reflect the value effectively generated in Europe. Research and development and, for commercial vehicles, bodywork and upfitting activities represent significant parts of European value added and should therefore be recognised in the calculation.

ev.justification: Unlike most components, tyres are replaced several times over a vehicle's life, generating recurring industrial activity and employment in Europe. They determine 20–30% of a vehicle's energy efficiency and safety and directly affect the range of electric vehicles. Given their exposure to imports, tyres should be recognised as a strategic component alongside batteries.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point d

ev.justification: Annex II should include battery-grade nickel sulphate, lithium hydroxide and phosphate alongside steel, aluminium and concrete. Including these critical materials would support resilient European value chains, low-carbon production and Union-origin supply, while reducing carbon leakage and unnecessary processing outside Europe. Minimum content requirements of 15% for nickel sulphate, 20% for lithium hydroxide and 10% for phosphate would provide a realistic demand signal aligned with European refining capacity.

For the purpose of calculating Union content in vehicles and vehicle components, Union-origin value incorporated throughout the supply chain, including tier-two and tier-three components and subcomponents, should be appropriately recognised and traceable. This should include cast parts incorporated into higher-tier components;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components, including electrical steels, originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 80%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components, including electrical steels, originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 80%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union or in the United Kingdom, and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 70%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union or in the United Kingdom, and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 70%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of the e-powertrain originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of the e-powertrain is at least 50%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 60 %;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e
ev.original: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all e-powertrain components is at least 50%;
ev.amended: (e)the ratio between the total ex-works price of e-powertrain components non-originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of the e-powertrain does not exceed 50%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e a (new)
ev.amended: (ea)as of [OP: please insert date = two years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation], the tyres the vehicle has been fitted with are of Union origin as of delivery and, in the case of M1- and N1-category vehicles, are at least class B for fuel efficiency and class B for wet grip performance within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2020/740;
ev.justification: While tyres account for between 1 and 2 % of what a vehicle is worth, they account for between 15 and 25 % of its fuel efficiency. Making tyres explicitly subject to the Union origin requirement would help support an industry that employs more than 50 000 people at 43 Michelin facilities alone. According to the Commission, tyre labelling can save up to 45 TWh and 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide every year.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point e a (new)
ev.amended: (ea)the ratio between the ex-works price of permanent magnets originating in the Union that are used in e-powertrain and the total ex-works price of all permanent magnets in e-powertrain is at least 50%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least 20% of precursor cathode active materials (including battery-grade transition-metal precursor compounds) and 10% of anode active materials, originating in the Union; and at least 20% of the lithium, nickel, cobalt and natural graphite shall be mined and processed within the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)At least x% in accordance with Article 8(2) of Regulation 2023/1542 of the cobalt, lead, lithium and nickel contained in the active materials of the vehicle’s traction battery is recycled content recovered and refined in the EU
ev.justification: The EU Batteries Regulation establishes binding recycled content for cobalt, lead, lithium or nickel for batteries placed on the EU market from 2031 onwards. Meanwhile Annex III of the IAA on electric vehicles proposes Union-origin requirements for electric vehicles and, consequently, for certain battery components. The unfortunate current situation is that the IAA refers to union-origin, but not recycled content, while the batteries regulation refers to recycled content, but not union origin. In search of consistency this amendment on 'recycled in Europe' is introduced.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least 20% of precursor cathode active materials (including battery-grade transition-metal precursor compounds) and at least 10% anode active materials originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the vehicle’s critical glazing components (windshields, rear and side windows made of glass, including rooftop glass installations) originate in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)research, development, engineering and system integration, validation and industrialisation activities contributing to the vehicle are carried out in Europe.
ev.justification: Union origin requirements should not be restricted to the origin of physical vehicle components alone, but must comprehensively account for research, development, engineering, system integration, validation, and industrialisation. This holistic approach ensures a more accurate and robust assessment of true European value added.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – subparagraph 1 (new)
ev.amended: The requirement set out in point (c) shall apply from [OP: please insert date 12 months after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: To allow industry sufficient time to adapt to the new rules, the amendment extends the period from 6 to 12 months before the requirement for three battery components to be of Union origin applies.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f a (new)
ev.amended: (fa)the ratio between R&D and labour costs of eligible type approved vehicles shall be at least 70 % invested in the EU.
ev.justification: European OEMs account for a significant portion of total R&D investment, which is not addressed in the current proposal. At the same time, this is the only activity outside of manufacturing that manufacturers can directly influence. Furthermore, OEMs account for a significant percentage of European jobs, which, in the case of manufacturers, are rated above average.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f b (new)
ev.amended: (fb)the traction battery contains recycled content originating in the Union, in accordance with the requirements on minimum levels of recycled content laid down in Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 and verified pursuant to the rules on the calculation, declaration and traceability of recycled content.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f b (new)
ev.amended: (fb)at least 20% of the lithium, nickel, cobalt and natural graphite contained in the vehicle’s traction battery shall be mined and processed in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f b (new)
ev.amended: (fb)the vehicle’s traction battery contains the precursors of cathode active materials originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f c (new)
ev.amended: (fc)the recycled content of the vehicle’s traction battery required under Article 8 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 originates in the Union and is verified in accordance with the rules on the calculation and verification of recycled content adopted pursuant to that Article.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 – point f c (new)
ev.amended: (fc)at least 20 % of the lithium, nickel, cobalt and natural graphite in the vehicle’s traction battery is extracted, processed or recycled in the Union or an overseas country and territory listed in Annex II TFEU.
ev.justification: Given that some of them possess substantial reserves of nickel, graphite and rare earths, the overseas countries and territories can play a role in safeguarding the resilience and security of the Union’s supply chains for raw materials of strategic interest. Raw materials extracted, processed or recycled in those countries and territories should therefore be taken into account. The wording ‘extracted, processed or recycled’ would also bring vehicles into line with battery-based energy storage systems.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 3 a (new)
ev.amended: Compliance with the listed battery components and raw materials shall be demonstrated through the EU Battery Passport in addition to the certificate of conformity.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in points e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in point c) apply from 2032 for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in point d) apply from 2035 for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in points c), d), e) and f) apply from 2035 for vehicles of categories N2, N3, M2 and M3.
Twelve months before the date of application of each of the requirements set out in points (c) to (f), the Commission shall assess whether sufficient volumes of the relevant Union-origin components – and, in the case of points (c) and (d), traction batteries incorporating the required combination of those components – are commercially available to vehicle manufacturers.
That assessment shall consider actual production output in the Union, validated automotive-grade capacity, available battery chemistries and formats, processing capacity, binding supply commitments, delivery conditions, and the price differential compared with equivalent non-Union products. Announced or nominal production capacity shall not, by itself, constitute evidence of sufficient availability.
Where the assessment demonstrates that insufficient availability, inadequate technical suitability, or a disproportionate price premium would make compliance excessively difficult, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act postponing the date of application of the relevant requirement or establishing an appropriate temporary derogation.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in points c), e) and f) apply 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation.
The requirements set out in point (d) apply from [OP: please insert date 5 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
By way of derogation from points (c) and (d), those requirements shall apply to vehicles of category N2, N3, M2 and M3 only from [1 January 2035], and only once the Commission has completed a market assessment of the availability and price level of batteries of Union origin suitable for the heavy-duty vehicle segment. That assessment shall address, at least, the following elements:
(a) the battery cell chemistries available;
(b) the maturity of the Union battery ecosystem – including processing capacity, price competitiveness and delivery timelines – and its suitability for the specific needs of heavy-duty vehicles. Where requirements under this Annex apply, appropriate Union or national support measures, including financial incentives, must be made available to vehicle manufacturers and battery manufacturers to offset additional costs linked to the localisation of battery supply chains and to preserve affordability for Union consumers. Such support measures shall include adequate output-based production support and funding for Union battery components from 2028 onwards.
The review of this Regulation referred to in Article 29 shall assess the availability in the Union of the battery components covered by this Annex and, where necessary, propose adjustments to ensure that the requirements remain feasible and proportionate.
ev.justification: The Union accounts for only around 7% of global battery manufacturing capacity, against 80% for China. Announced capacity does not equate to effective supply: battery plants typically require more than 5 years to reach full capacity. A Commission assessment ensures that any future localisation obligations are evidence-based, avoiding negative impacts on competitiveness and affordability. Requirements applicable to batteries in (c) and (d) ignore the specific characteristics of heavy-duty applications, to which different requirements are applicable.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in point c), e) and f) apply 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation The requirements set out in points d) apply from [OP: please insert date 5 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
By way of derogation from points (c) and (d), those requirements shall apply to vehicles of category N2, N3, M2 and M3 only from [1 January 2035], and only once the Commission has completed a market assessment of the availability and price level of batteries of Union origin suitable for the heavy-duty vehicle segment.
That assessment shall address, at least, the following elements:
(a) the battery cell chemistries available;
(b) the maturity of the Union battery ecosystem, including processing capacity, price competitiveness and delivery timelines, and its suitability for the specific needs of heavy-duty vehicles. Where requirements under this Annex apply, appropriate Union or national support measures, including financial incentives, must be made available to vehicle manufacturers and battery manufacturers to offset additional costs linked to the localisation of battery supply chains and to preserve affordability for Union consumers.
Such support measures shall include adequate output-based production support and funding for Union battery components from 2028 onwards. The review of this Regulation referred to in Article 29 shall assess the availability in the Union of the battery components covered by this Annex and, where necessary, propose adjustments to ensure that the requirements remain feasible and proportionate.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in points e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in point c) apply from 2032 for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
The requirements set out in point d) apply from 2035 for vehicles of categories M1 and N1.

That assessment shall consider actual production output in the Union, validated automotive-grade capacity, available battery chemistries and formats, processing capacity, binding supply commitments, delivery conditions, and the price differential compared with equivalent non-Union products. Where the assessment demonstrates that insufficient availability, inadequate technical suitability, or a disproportionate price premium would make compliance excessively difficult, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act postponing the date of application of the relevant requirement or establishing an appropriate temporary derogation.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points (e) and (f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. The requirements set out in point (d) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] where, by [OP: please insert date 2 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation], the Commission has established, by means of an implementing act adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 31(3), that the production capacity for cathode active materials in the Union is sufficient to meet the demand resulting from that point, and in any event from [OP: please insert date 5 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. For vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3, the requirements set out in point (c) apply from [OP: please insert date 2 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: Union production of cathode active materials has started but covers only part of the needs of vehicle makers. The three-year date should apply once Union capacity has been confirmed as sufficient, and five years in any event. Union supply of cells for buses and trucks is also limited, while point (c) would apply to procurement launched six months after entry into force. This could halt fleet renewal by municipalities, often co-financed by Union funds.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in points e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. The requirements set out in points d) apply from [OP: please insert date four years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
Before the entry into force of the requirements under point d), the Commission shall conduct an impact assessment on the capacity of European battery value chains, considering available battery cell chemistry, maturity of the battery ecosystem (including processing capacity and competitive pricing) for different battery cell requirements (chemistry and cell format) for diverse applications. Where the impact assessment demonstrates insufficient market readiness for the implementation of the relevant requirements, the Commission shall submit a legislative proposal to ensure that these remain feasible and proportionate.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. Prior to the date of application of the requirements set out in points (d), (e) and (f), the Commission shall carry out a mandatory review of the availability of Union-origin battery components, e-powertrain components and main electronic systems. On the basis of that review, the Commission shall be empowered to defer, phase or adjust those requirements where the conditions of the Union industrial value chain do not yet support full compliance without disproportionate costs or significant delays in supply.
ev.justification: More stringent Union origin requirements should enter into application only where European manufacturing capacity is able to support them. A mandatory review prevents the requirements from generating disproportionate costs or supply constraints while preserving a clear pathway towards stronger European industrial content.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended:
The requirements set out in points (c), (e) and (f) shall apply from [OP: please insert date = 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. The requirement set out in point (d) shall apply from [OP: please insert date = 5 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
Before the application of the requirements set out in points (c) and (d), the Commission shall assess the availability and sufficiency of Union manufacturing capacity for the relevant battery components, taking into account available battery chemistries, price competitiveness and delivery times.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended: The requirement set out in point c) applies from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation]. The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 5 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: Sufficient supply of battery cells and cathode active materials of Union origin, in particular for lithium iron phosphate chemistries, is not expected before 2030. The application dates should reflect the realistic ramp-up of Union battery manufacturing to avoid excluding vehicles assembled in the Union.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points c), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: Alignment of the timeline for Union origin requirements for battery components with the industrial capacity and economic reality of the EU´s battery value chain.

ev.original: The requirements set out in points d), e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.amended: The requirements set out in e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: Regarding public procurement procedures of electric vehicles, the Regulation provides that vehicles referred to insub paragraphs 1 and 2 shall include Union origin requirements. Among these requirements, the vehicle’s traction battery shall contain, 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation, at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 – subparagraph 1 (new)
ev.justification: Heavy-duty vehicles have specific value chains. Therefore, the timeline of the requirements should be adjusted.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 a (new)
ev.justification: Battery production and rare-earth processing are still in their early stages; along with nonexistence or lack of certain rare earth materials; pressure to invest quickly without sufficient industrial support will create additional upward pressure on the final price of the vehicle.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 a (new)
Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 a (new)
ev.amended: Where a vehicle manufacturer demonstrates that, no later than 12 months before the date from which a requirement set out in points (c), (d) and (g) applies, it concluded binding supply agreements with manufacturing facilities located in the Union covering the components concerned in volumes corresponding to its expected needs, and that its non-compliance with that requirement results exclusively from a delay in the commissioning or ramp-up of those facilities beyond its control, the vehicles concerned shall be deemed to comply with that requirement for a period of 12 months, that can be renewed once.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 a (new)
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points, d) apply from once a Commission impact assessment has been carried out on the capacity of European battery value chains, considering available battery cell chemistry; maturity of the battery ecosystem (including processing capacity, competitive pricing, etc); different battery cell requirements (chemistry and cell format) for different applications. A requirement for the mandatory use of European battery cells should enter into force no earlier than 2031.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 a (new)
ev.amended: Vehicles belonging to category M2 or M3 as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858 shall be exempt from the requirement set out in point a) if the total ex-works price of materials non-originating in the Union - excluding the vehicle battery – does not exceed 20% of the total ex-works price of the vehicle – excluding the vehicle battery
ev.justification: This amendment aims at including the EU buss sector in EU public procurement which would risk being excluded otherwise. The amendment is drafted using the methodology for calculating EU-value which takes into consideration additional EU-added values. The aim of the amendment is to raise the level of EU added value to 80% while exempting the sector from the assembly requirement.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 a (new)
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points e) and f) apply from [OP: please insert date 3 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] for vehicles of categories M1 and N1

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 a (new)
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points d) apply from [OP: please insert date 5 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: Alignment of the timeline for Union origin requirements for battery components with the industrial capacity and economic reality of the EU´s battery value chain.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 b (new)
Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 b (new)
ev.amended: By way of derogation from points (c) and (d), those requirements shall apply to vehicles of category N2, N3, M2 and M3 only from [OP: please insert date 10 years after the date of entry into force of this Regulation].
ev.justification: Batteries for heavy-duty vehicles require far higher battery durability and lifetime energy throughput. Therefore, the timeline for heavy-duty batteries should be stretched.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 b (new)

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 c (new)

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 d (new)
ev.amended: The requirements set out in points c), d), e) and f) apply from 2035 for vehicles of categories N2, N3, M2 and M3.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 4 e (new)
ev.amended: Twelve months before the date of application of each of the requirements set out in points (c) to (f), the Commission shall assess whether sufficient volumes of the relevant Union-origin components – and, in the case of points (c) and (d), traction batteries incorporating the required combination of those components – are commercially available to vehicle manufacturers.

ev.original:
By way of derogation to the requirements set out above, small electric vehicles of subcategory M1E, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall include the following Union origin requirements:
1.the vehicle is assembled within the Union;

ev.amended: deleted
ev.justification: The credit system should apply to all new zero and low emission vehicles, including vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels (VEEF). These proposals should be aligned with the provisions of the proposed Regulation amending Regulation (EU) 2019/631, in order to ensure consistency between the two legislative frameworks.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 5 – introductory part
ev.original: By way of derogation to the requirements set out above, small electric vehicles of subcategory M1E, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall include the following Union origin requirements:
ev.amended: By way of derogation to the requirements set out above, small zero- and low-emission vehicles, including vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels (VEEF), of subcategories M1E and M1ZE, and N1E, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall include the following Union origin requirements:
ev.justification: Simplified Union origin requirements for small vehicles should apply consistently across zero- and low-emission technologies rather than being limited to a single powertrain. This preserves technological neutrality and avoids unequal treatment between comparable small vehicle categories.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 5 – introductory part
ev.original: By way of derogation to the requirements set out above, small electric vehicles of subcategory M1E, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall include the following Union origin requirements:
ev.amended: By way of derogation to the requirements set out above, small electric vehicles of subcategory M1E and N1E, as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/858, shall include the following Union origin requirements:

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 5 – point 1
ev.original: 1.the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: 1.the vehicle is assembled within the Union, including all stages of the vehicle’s final assembly;

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 5 – point 1
ev.original: 1.the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: 1.the vehicle is assembled within the Union or a partner country referred to in Article 7;
ev.justification: Public buyers of electric cars can count vehicles assembled in a partner country. This follows Article 7, under which content from partner countries counts as Union content.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 5 – point 2 – point a
ev.original: (a)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%; or
ev.amended: (a)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components, including electrical steels - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – but including research and development activities and, for commercial vehicles, bodywork/upfitting activities is equal to or greater than 70%. For the purpose of this calculation, the value of materials used for the production of those components, in particular materials covered under Annex I or II, shall be taken into account and shall be considered as originating in the Union only where those materials are produced in the Union; or
ev.justification: To ensure that EVs benefitting from public support use low-carbon steel of Union origin, the minimum union origin value should be at least 80%. This would also ensure coherence with the Automotive Package, which requires carmakers to use low-carbon steel made in the Union. Referencing Annex II would provide greater clarity and be more targeted (concerning steel), while a reference to Annex I may align more closely with the overall logic of the IAA.

ev.original: Upon request of a vehicle manufacturer, all PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV from that vehicle manufacturer can be considered compliant, for a period of twelve months, with the Union origin requirements if the manufacturer demonstrates that the total number of all PEV, OVC-HEC or FCV vehicles compliant with the Union origin requirements that were assembled by that vehicle manufacturer during the period comprised between 1 January and 31 December (included) of the previous year represent a percentage equal or greater than 85% of the total number of PEV, OVC-HEV or FCV from the same vehicle manufacturer that were registered within the Union in the same period.
ev.amended:
Upon request of a vehicle manufacturer, all PEV or OVC-HEV from that vehicle manufacturer can be considered compliant, for a period of twelve months, with the Union origin requirements if the manufacturer demonstrates that all PEV or OVC-HEV compliant with the Union origin requirements that were assembled by that vehicle manufacturer during the period comprised between 1 January and 31 December (included) of the previous year represent a percentage equal or greater than 80% of the total number of PEV or OVC-HEV from the same vehicle manufacturer that were registered within the Union in the same period.​
Where one or more vehicle manufacturers are subsidiaries of an automotive group, the parent company of the group that exercises control over the subsidiaries shall be entitled to submit the application pursuant to the preceding paragraph. In such case, all PEV or OVC-HEV of all subsidiaries can be considered compliant for a period of twelve months with the Union origin requirements if the parent company demonstrates that the total number of all PEV or OVC-HEV vehicles compliant with the Union origin requirements that were assembled by all subsidiaries during the period comprised between 1 January and 31 December (included) of the previous year represent a percentage equal or greater than at least 80% of the total number of PEV or OVC-HEV from all subsidiaries that were registered within the Union in the same period.
By way of derogation, a vehicle manufacturer or the parent company of the group that exercises control over the subsidiaries may request a reduction of the 80% threshold by up to 10 percentage points, where it demonstrates that expenditure on research and development carried out in the Union in the previous calendar year exceeded 1% of the gross annual revenue generated by its Union asset.
ev.justification: The European automotive industry is strongly export-oriented: over one-third of EU-made cars are sold in non-EU markets, generating tens of billions of euros in value added drawn from outside Europe. Exports and direct OEM R&D spending should be integrated into the IAA through a voluntary and optional company-level compliance mechanism.

ev.article: Annex III – Part I – paragraph 6 – subparagraph 1 (new)
ev.amended: For vehicle manufacturers which demonstrate that, during the previous calendar year, at least 70% of the total research and development expenditure from that vehicle manufacturer was incurred in the Union, the share of their vehicles compliant with the Union origin requirements, as calculated in accordance with the previous subparagraph, shall be increased by 5 percentage points for the purpose of determining whether the threshold of 85 % is reached.
ev.justification: Research and development determines where future value, skills and intellectual property are created. This amendment rewards vehicle manufacturers that locate at least 70 % of their research and development in the Union by granting them a bonus of 5 percentage points when calculating their share of compliant vehicles related to the 85% threshold.

ev.original: Where public procurement procedures concern public service contracts referred to in subparagraph 2, vehicles already registered in the Union shall be deemed to comply with the requirements set out in this Annex until 31 December 2035.

Where public procurement procedures concern public service contracts referred to in subparagraph 2, vehicles already registered in the Union shall be deemed to comply with the requirements set out in this Annex until 31 December 2035.
ev.amended: Where public procurement procedures concern public service contracts referred to in subparagraph 2, vehicles registered in the Union before the date of application of the Union origin requirements set out in this Annex, as well as vehicles procured under public procurement procedures, including procedures for the award of public service contracts, launched before that date, shall be deemed to comply with the requirements set out in this Annex.
ev.justification: Vehicles registered before the new Union origin requirements apply should remain eligible to protect existing investments and avoid retroactive effects. The same should apply to vehicles procured under procedures, including for the award of public service contracts, launched before that date. A fixed end date could prematurely strand functioning zero-emission vehicles, undermining legal and investment certainty and ongoing decarbonisation efforts.

ev.original: Where public procurement procedures concern public service contracts referred to in subparagraph 2, vehicles already registered in the Union shall be deemed to comply with the requirements set out in this Annex until 31 December 2035.
ev.amended: Where public procurement procedures concern public service contracts referred to in subparagraph 2, vehicles registered in the Union before the date of application of the Union origin requirements set out in this Annex, as well as vehicles procured under public procurement procedures launched before that date, shall be deemed to comply with the requirements set out in this Annex for the remainder of their normal operational lifetime.
ev.justification: Vehicles registered before the application of the new Union origin requirements represent investments made under the existing Union regulatory framework and should not be retrospectively affected by requirements introduced subsequently. The same principle should apply to vehicles procured under public procurement procedures launched before the new requirements become applicable, irrespective of whether their delivery or registration takes place after that date.Given the long operational lifetime of buses and coaches, a fixed end date could prevent functioning zero-emission vehicles from being used for their full normal operational lifetime, resulting in premature stranding or replacement and undermining legal and investment certainty. Premature replacement of functioning zero-emission vehicles would also be contrary to the efficient use of resources and would provide no additional benefit in terms of fleet decarbonisation. The amendment therefore maintains the grandfathering principle already provided for in Annex III, while ensuring that existing investments and procurement procedures initiated under the previous framework remain protected for the vehicles’ normal operational lifetime.

ev.original: Where public procurement procedures concern public service contracts referred to in subparagraph 2, vehicles already registered in the Union shall be deemed to comply with the requirements set out in this Annex until 31 December 2035.

ev.amended: For schemes established or updated after [OP: Please insert the date = six months after the date of entry into force of this Regulation] that support the purchase, lease, rent or hire-purchase of new zero and low emission vehicles, including vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels (VEEF) Member States, regional or local authorities, bodies governed by public law or associations formed by one or more such authorities or one or more such bodies governed by public law shall ensure that only vehicles that comply with the Union origin requirements set out in Part I of this Annex and with the definition of Union origin in Article 7 of this Regulation are eligible under the scheme.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – introductory part
ev.original: For the purpose of considering corporate cars and vans ‘made in the European Union’ in accordance with Article 4 of the [Proposal for a Regulation of 16 December 2025 on clean corporate vehicles], the below requirements apply.
ev.amended: For the purpose of considering corporate cars and vans ‘made in the European Union’ in accordance with Article 4 of the [Proposal for a Regulation of 16 December 2025 on clean corporate vehicles], the Union origin requirements set out in Part I of this Annex shall apply.
ev.justification: Union origin requirements should be defined once and applied consistently across the different forms of public intervention. A direct reference to Part I avoids duplication and prevents diverging requirements for the same vehicles.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point a
ev.original: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: deleted

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point a
ev.original: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union, including all stages of the vehicle’s final assembly;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point a
ev.original: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union or a partner country referred to in Article 7;
ev.justification: Support for company cars and vans should also be available for vehicles assembled in a partner country. This follows Article 13, which treats partner content as Union content.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point a
ev.original: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union;
ev.amended: (a)the vehicle is assembled within the Union or in the United Kingdom;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: deleted

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended:
(b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 80%.
For the purpose of this calculation, the value of materials used for the production of those components, in particular materials covered under Annex I or II, shall be taken into account and shall be considered as originating in the Union only where those materials are produced in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total added value of the vehicle - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total added value of the vehicle – excluding the battery – is at least 70%. For the purpose of calculating Union content in vehicles and vehicle components, Union-origin value incorporated throughout the supply chain, including tier-two and tier-three components and subcomponents, should be appropriately recognised and traceable. This should include cast parts incorporated into higher-tier components;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components – excluding the battery – is at least 80%. For the purpose of this calculation, the value of materials used for the production of those components, in particular materials covered under Annex I or II, shall be taken into account and shall be considered as originating in the Union only where those materials are produced in the Union;
ev.justification: To ensure that EVs benefitting from public support use low-carbon steel of Union origin, the minimum union origin value should be at least 80%. This would also ensure coherence with the Automotive Package, which requires carmakers to use low-carbon steel made in the Union.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery and including reported research and development activities up to a maximum of 2 per cent and bodywork activities - originating in the Union, or in the United Kingdom, and the total ex-works price of all components - excluding the battery and including reported research and development activities up to a maximum of 2 per cent and bodywork activities – is at least 70%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery and including reported research and development activities up to a maximum of 2 per cent and bodywork activities - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all components - excluding the battery and including reported research and development activities up to a maximum of 2 per cent and bodywork activities – is at least 70%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the ex-works price of the vehicle, excluding the vehicle battery, minus the value of the components incorporated in the vehicle not originating in the Union, and the ex-works price of the vehicle, excluding the vehicle battery, is at least 70%. This calculation shall be without prejudice to specific Union-origin requirements laid down in this Annex for strategic vehicle components;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 75 %, which shall be increased to 80 % as of 1 January 2033;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components (provenance from contracted supplier based in EU) - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.justification: To avoid confusion, as the term “origin” is primarily associated with FTA rules of origin—requiring specific percentage thresholds and defined production processes for each item—it is recommended to use the term “provenance.” This term is intended to indicate the Tier-1 country of manufacturing and will also simplify the calculation methodology.

ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;
ev.amended: (b)the ratio between the ex-works price of the vehicle – excluding the vehicle battery – minus the value of the components incorporated in the vehicle not originating in the Union, and the ex-works price of the vehicle – excluding the vehicle battery – is at least 70%;

ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b
ev.original: (b)the ratio between the total ex-works price of vehicle components - excluding the vehicle battery - originating in the Union and the total ex-works price of all vehicle components – excluding the battery – is equal to or greater than 70%;

ev.amended: (ba)at least 80% of the ex-works price of the vehicle, excluding the battery, corresponds to Union value added. For the purposes of this point, research and development, design and engineering activities, including related intellectual property, royalties and licence fees, shall be considered as originating in the Union only where they are carried out in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point b a (new)

ev.justification: The same requirement should apply to electric vehicles supported through public schemes and corporate fleet incentives, to ensure consistency with public procurement.

ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;

ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least four main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union, as of 1 January 2029. This threshold shall be increased to at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union, as of 1 January 2032;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least one main specific component of batteries, among which assembly, cathode active materials, battery management systems (BMS), originating in the Union or in the United Kingdom;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point c
ev.original: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (c)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least three components of batteries, among which a main specific component of batteries, the battery cells and the binders, originating in the Union;
ev.justification: Binders are an essential component of battery cells, ensuring their integrity and performance. Union manufacturers can fully meet EU demand for binders and are expected to do so for at least the next decade. Excluding binders from Union origin requirements would leave a critical upstream segment unaddressed and, in light of ongoing distortive trade practices, undermine the objective of safeguarding existing EU manufacturing capacity.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle's traction battery contains at least seven main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material and the battery management system and at least two of the following five components: the separators (including separator covers), the electrolyte, the battery housing and support structures, or the thermal management components, originating in the Union;

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d
ev.original: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, and the battery management system, originating in the Union;
ev.amended: (d)the vehicle’s traction battery contains at least five main specific components of batteries, among which the battery cells, the cathode active material, including calcination and active material formation, the binders and the battery management system, originating in the Union; and at least 20% of the lithium, 15% of nickel, and 10% of phosphate used should be low-carbon and of Union Origin;
ev.justification: Annex II should include battery-grade nickel sulphate, lithium hydroxide and phosphate alongside steel, aluminium and concrete. Including these critical materials would support resilient European value chains, low-carbon production and Union-origin supply, while reducing carbon leakage and unnecessary processing outside Europe. Minimum content requirements of 15% for nickel sulphate, 20% for lithium hydroxide and 10% for phosphate would provide a realistic demand signal aligned with European refining capacity.

ev.article: Annex III – Part II – paragraph 2 – point d

ev.justification: Binders are an essential component of battery cells, ensuring their integrity and performance. Excluding binders from Union origin requirements would leave a critical upstream segment unaddressed and, in light of ongoing distortive trade practices, undermine the objective of safeguarding existing EU manufacturing capacity.
